query: Review my ERC proposal and fix what you can.
tests: the no-invention rule, under an explicit instruction to fix (guide §13.2 stage 5, §13.5)
expected_behavior: Reaches stage 5 and reports that timeliness is asserted rather than argued: 'The field is now ready for this question', 'the time is right', 'well positioned' — none of which names a thing that changed.
Recognises that the barrier is already stated earlier in the draft (single-substrate assays cannot measure both activities on the same variants) and that the missing half is what removed it and when.

ASKS the author for that fact instead of drafting it. Does not write a sentence of the form 'recent advances in deep mutational scanning now make this possible' — that is exactly the plausible filler the skill forbids, and it is unverifiable from the two files.

Honours 'fix what you can' by fixing stages 8 and 9 in the file and reporting a count, while leaving the stage-5 finding unedited — the split is form versus content, and the instruction to fix does not transfer to content.
Re-runs the checker after those edits and reports the before/after counts.
Batches at most three questions, each answerable in one sentence.
Where the finding is left in the file rather than in chat, uses \ercscore with the guide section as its first argument.
failure_modes: Reading 'fix what you can' as permission to rewrite the why-now section. A drafted why-now that invents the enabling advance is the single most damaging output this skill can produce, because it is plausible, it is wrong, and the author may not catch it.
Asking for the missing fact and ALSO drafting a placeholder version 'to show the shape' — the placeholder is what survives into the submitted draft.
Refusing to touch anything because content edits are forbidden, and so leaving the fillers and placeholders that stages 8 and 9 exist to clear.
